title: France – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Solution SaaS - Programmation et optimisation des flux entrants du processus logistique
description: Le centre de services Logistique Industrielle (LI), rattaché à la Direction des Services Supports (DIR2S) d’Enedis souhaite se doter d'une solution SaaS clé en main, permettant la planification, l’optimisation, le pilotage et la traçabilité des flux de livraison en entrée des sites logistiques, au service de la performance opérationnelle des sites logistiques et de la chaîne d’approvisionnement. Au-delà des fonctions de planification, la solution devra constituer un véritable outil de pilotage de l’activité, en intégrant des capacités avancées d’analyse, de reporting et de valorisation des données. Elle doit permettre une vision consolidée, fiable et exploitable des flux de livraison fournisseur, à la fois à la maille de chaque site logistique et au niveau national, afin de faciliter la prise de décision, l’anticipation des charges et l’amélioration continue des processus. Montant maximum du marché : 869 000 € HT. Le présent marché est mono attributaire. 5 candidats maximum seront retenues pour participer à la phase de consultation. Durée ferme du marché: 3 ans. reconduction : 5 fois un an. La date de début du marché est estimée au : 26/04/2027.

title: France – Parts of railway or tramway locomotives or rolling stock; railways traffic-control equipment – Système de mesure automatisée des roues de tramway au défilé (SMAR) : fourniture, installation, mise en service et maintien en conditions opérationnelles, ligne T2 et lignes de tramway fer de la RATP
description: Le présent avis vise à mettre en place un marché mono-titulaire, non alloti, à minimum et maximum exprimés en quantités, exécuté par ordres de livraison et de service, ayant pour objet, pour chaque site équipé : la conception, la fourniture, l'installation et la mise en service d'un dispositif de mesure au défilé du profil des roues de tramway (capteurs laser, caméras, éclairage, armoire, modules de traitement et de communication) ; la fourniture, le paramétrage et la mise en service du logiciel de reconstruction et d'exploitation des profils de roues et son intégration au système d'information de maintenance de la RATP ; l'étude d'implantation et les prestations d'intégration sur l'infrastructure ; les essais, la validation métrologique et l'accompagnement d'une période probatoire de six mois ; la documentation en français et la formation des mainteneurs ; la garantie de trois ans à compter de la réception définitive, incluant la maintenance du dispositif et du logiciel ; la fourniture de pièces de rechange et la gestion de l'obsolescence (disponibilité garantie quinze ans) ; sur commande, la maintenance post-garantie. Minimum (engagement ferme) : équipement de la ligne T2, soit deux (2) dispositifs en voie de remisage des sites de maintenance et de remisage d'Issy-les-Moulineaux et de Colombes, avec le logiciel, la mise en service, la vérification de service régulier et la garantie de trois ans à compter de la réception définitive. Maximum : huit (8) dispositifs au total sur l'ensemble des lignes de tramway fer (T1, T2, T3a, T3b, T7, T8), le raccordement de cinq lignes supplémentaires au logiciel, la maintenance post-garantie des huit dispositifs et du logiciel jusqu'au terme du marché, la capacité de mesure des roues de 370 mm pour huit dispositifs (ligne optionnelle) et les prestations d'expertise technique, dans la limite des quantités maximales de l'article 17 du projet de marché. Les travaux préparatoires d'acheminement des réseaux et le génie civil sont réalisés par la RATP hors marché.

title: Gutter Cleaning and Maintenance Services
description: 27-RFP-ROICC-0008 - Gutter Cleaning and Maintenance Services at Naval Weapons Station Earle, Colts Neck, NJ This notice is being issued strictly for Market Research, information and planning and purposes only and shall not be construed as either a solicitation or obligation or commitment on the part of the Government. There will not be a solicitation, specifications, or drawings available at this time. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to help The Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC), Naval Weapons Station Earle (NWSE), understand industry best practices and sources capable of meeting the requirements detailed by this announcement. NWSE welcomes responses from all interested parties; however, no decision or award of contract will be made based on responses from industry. NWSE will not pay for the preparation of, nor the subsequent use of information submitted in response to this Sources Sought. Respondents will not be notified of the outcome of NWSE�s review of the information received. Additionally, NWSE does not intend to hold discussions concerning this Sources Sought with any interested parties, but reserves the right to contact contractors if additional information is required for clarifications as it pertains to this request for information (RFI). Requirement: The source of this requirement is NAVFAC, Naval Weapons Station (NWS) Earle Requirements Branch and the Facilities Services Branch, located in Colts Neck, NJ. The requirement is for Maintenance and Repair of Gutters and Downspouts Services at NWS Earle in Colts Neck, NJ. Contractor shall perform gutter maintenance to ensure proper gutter and down spout drainage operation during the year. The Contractor shall maintain gutters in proper condition and operation; gutters are properly pitched and correctly attached and draining away from the building; maintain gutters so they do not leak to include seams and corners; clean gutters removing debris and disposing of off station. To that end, NWSE seeks to gather information about sources able to meet this requirement. The NAICS Code for this requirement is 238170 (Siding Contractors). The associated small business size standard for this industry is $19,000,000.00. Instructions to Contractors: All interested contractors are encouraged to submit a response clearly demonstrating their capability to perform this requirement. Proposals are not being requested at this time. Responses to this Sources Sought cannot be considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a contract. No formal solicitation exists at this time and no set-aside decision has been made. Responses to this Sources Sought should include the following information: Provide documentation that explicitly demonstrates the capacity and capability of satisfying the Government�s requirements. This may include contract numbers, locations, and (if available) points of contact for previous similar work. The capabilities statement should be brief and concise; do not exceed five single sided pages, double spaced, 12 pt. font. Provide statement of the contractor�s socioeconomic status (i.e. SB, 8(a), HubZone, EDWOSB, WOSB, SDVOSB, etc) and size. Please submit responses by 6 November 2026 11:00AM EST directly to Joseph Henrius, Contracting Officer, via email at joseph.p.henrius.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the Sources Sought number (27-RFP-ROICC-0008) and title in the subject (Gutter Cleaning and Maintenance Services) of your message. title: GLQ and TDY apartment cleaning services
description: The U.S. Embassy in Madrid plans to issue Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. 19SP5027Q0002 for cleaning services. The work covers about 110 Government-leased apartments and single-family homes in central Madrid and its suburbs, plus one temporary duty (TDY) apartment. Services include cleaning leased residences before a new resident moves in, cleaning the TDY apartment after each guest leaves, and weekly touch-up cleaning of the TDY apartment during guest stays. The contractor will provide all labor, supervision, supplies and equipment, except for limited items the Government provides. The Government plans to award multiple firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts. Each contract will have a 12-month base period and three 12-month option periods. Prices will be in euros. The Government will award to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offerors that it finds responsible. Offerors must: Operate an established business with a permanent address and telephone listing in Madrid, Spain. Hold all licenses and permits required under Spanish law. Have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) before award. Show relevant past performance providing comparable services in Spain. Provide a Project Manager who understands written and spoken English. Carry the minimum insurance specified in the solicitation. The RFQ will be posted on SAM.gov about mid-November. Interested parties should watch SAM.gov for the solicitation and any amendments. This notice is not a request for quotations, and the Government will not accept quotations in response to it. Electronic Submission/Responses: No electronic offers will be accepted. Please mail or hand-delivery your offer to the contracting office that will be included in the solicitation.

title: Leighton Linslade Town Council Waste Contract
description: This is an excellent opportunity to work with the award winning Leighton Linslade Town Council running our waste contract across 5 sites in our portfolio. We are a Town Council who prides themselves on our Biodiversity and Ecology work and the new waste contractor must also be able to demonstrate their work around protecting the environment for future generations to enjoy. title: Prototype development for Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination
description: This RPP is being issued by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), in support of the Defense Health Agency�s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Medical Products (MP) Warfighter Protection (WPAC) & Acute Care Program Management Office (PMO) Care located in Frederick, Maryland at Fort Detrick. The Warfighter Protection and Acute Care Project Management Office (WPAC PMO) has a requirement for the development of a Barrier Combination product. The Barrier Combination product is defined as being composed of both a physical barrier to protect a wound and an antibacterial and/or antifungal activity released from the barrier to prevent the spread of organisms and avoid systemic infections. This RPP will result in one award to develop the Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination (BC) prototype product. The final product MUST be a combination wound treatment that includes a barrier component that is either infused or impregnated with antimicrobial and/or antifungal properties and have U.S. Food Drug Administration (FDA) approval (or clearance). The award, as a result of this RPP, will be awarded under the authority of prototype Other Transaction Authority (pOTA) 10 U.S.C. 4022.

title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: **Note: Amendment 0003 is hereby posted on 10/14. Only those whom submitted timely Volumes I-III are eligible to submit the remaining Volume IV** The sources sought originally posted as W912HP27RA001 - Due to technical issues with ACWS a new solicitation number was pulled. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

description: This RPP is being issued by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), in support of the Defense Health Agency�s Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Medical Products (MP) Warfighter Protection (WPAC) & Acute Care Program Management Office (PMO) Care located in Frederick, Maryland at Fort Detrick. The Warfighter Protection and Acute Care Project Management Office (WPAC PMO) has a requirement for the development of a Barrier Combination product. The Barrier Combination product is defined as being composed of both a physical barrier to protect a wound and an antibacterial and/or antifungal activity released from the barrier to prevent the spread of organisms and avoid systemic infections. This RPP will result in one award to develop the Battlefield Wound Infection Prevention and Treatment (BWI P&T) Barrier Combination (BC) prototype product. title: E-6B Mission Computer Modernization (MCM) Software Licenses for Fiscal Year (FY) 27 and FY 28
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-271 Airborne Strategic Command, Control and Communications Program Office, intends to enter into negotiations and subsequently award to Rockwell Collins, Inc., doing business as Collins Aerospace Government Systems Division (CAGE Code: 13499), a modification to Delivery Order (DO) N0001925F0087 issued under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0001924G0017, to procure one (1) base year and one (1) option year of AGI Dynamic Geometry, Java SE, Jboss, MySQL, and Crossover software licenses required to support Mission Computer Modernization (MCM) efforts on the E-6B aircraft. The base licensing period will cover from 13 November 2026 through 12 November 2027, and the option licensing period will cover from 13 November 2027 through 12 November 2028. The software licenses are required to operate the system listed above. This action is anticipated to be greater than SAT. This action is not subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement (WTO GPA) and/or a Free Trade Agreement (FTA). This action is not anticipated to be awarded as a construction contract to a small business. This action does not require qualification requirements to be eligible for award. BOA N0001924G0017 was awarded sole source to Collins Aerospace under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1) as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1 prior to the Department of War implementation of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul Part 6, Class Deviation (CD) 2026-O0017, Revision 1, dated 23 January 2026. The modification to procure the software licenses described above will be executed under an existing delivery order N0001925F0087. The existing order requires Collins Aerospace to provide software support services related to mission system installation, operation, sustainment, development, integration, and testing on the E-6B aircraft systems for which Collins Aerospace is the Original Equipment Manufacturer, including the MCM. As such, Collins Aerospace possesses the technical data and specialized knowledge, including system architecture and compatibility requirements for the MCM, which is necessary to identify the exact version and quantity of software licenses required to support and operate that system. Award to any other source would result in unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. Any technical data associated with this action can be obtained through Collins Aerospace. This action is a result of the sources sought notice posted on 28 July 2026. This action will not be a small business set aside. description: See Soliciation Amendments 0001 and 0002. USAISR's Combat Casualty Care Research Team 1 (CRT-1) requires resupply of its Blood Donor Room on a reoccurring basis in order to satisfy research requirements for blood collection. The Contractor may engage qualified subcontractors to deliver executional services, where appropriate. The Contractor will remain fully responsible for the performance and quality of all services delivered by its subcontractors. See Statement of Work (Section C) for detailed requirements. It is DC’s intent to enter into an agreement with the proponent who can best serve the interests of DC. At the final outcome of the NRFP process, the successful proponent may be required to collaborate with DC’s other service providers and partners to ensure that public relations and communications services are consistent with DC’s mandate, brand and corporate strategy.

title: Fort Leavenworth Underground Fuel Tank Testing and Repair Services

The intention is to procure these services on a competitive basis. BASED ON THE REPSONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND THE MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUISNESS (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION. Disclaimer: This sources sought is for informational purposes only. This is not a �Request for Proposal (RFP)� to be submitted. It does not constitute as a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. PROGRAM BACKGROUND: Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, Department of Public Works (DPW) Environmental Division requires Underground Storage Tank Testing with Veeder Root systems to ensure compliance with Kansas Department of Health and Environment regulations. There are ten (10) underground fuel storage tanks on Fort Leavenworth equipment with Veeder Root 350+ or 450+ monitoring systems, spill buckets, and overfill valves. Information in sufficient detail regarding previous experience (either as a prime contractor or a subcontractor) on similar requirements (include size, scope, complexity, and whether government or commercial). 4. Information to determine if the service is commercially available, including pricing information, basis for the pricing information (e.g., market pricing, catalog pricing), and customary terms and conditions. 5. Evidence of certification from the Kansas Department of Health and Environment. 6. Identify how the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition, including competition among small business. 7. Recommendations to improve the Army�s approach/specifications/draft PWS. title: ISBEE Solicitation: Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal healthcare services for Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) services equivalent to two full-time CNMs at Rosebud Service Unit, Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota.
description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION � CERTIFIED NURSE-MIDWIFE SERVICES RFP No. 75H70627R00005 The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal Certified Nurse-Midwife (CNM) healthcare services at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. This requirement is set aside for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) under NAICS 561320, Temporary Help Services. The Contractor shall provide qualified CNM personnel sufficient to support two (2) full-time CNM positions providing outpatient obstetric, gynecological, prenatal, postpartum, family planning, and women�s primary care services, as well as obstetric emergency on-call coverage for the Emergency Department. The anticipated contract will use a Firm-Fixed-Price, Month-of-Service (MOS) pricing structure. One MOS represents complete monthly performance of the required CNM services in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The anticipated period of performance consists of a three (3)-month base period and three (3) option periods of three (3) months each, for a maximum potential period of performance of twelve (12) months. Services will be performed primarily at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. Standard outpatient clinic hours are generally Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The requirement also includes shared 24-hour-per-day, 7-day-per-week CNM on-call availability for obstetric emergencies during non-clinic hours. Offerors shall provide qualified personnel meeting the education, certification, licensure, credentialing, privileging, background investigation, health, and other qualification requirements identified in the PWS. The Government intends to make award to the responsible Offeror whose proposal conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the best value to the Government, price and other factors considered. Evaluation factors include Technical Capability, Past Performance, Management Approach, and Price. Applicable provisions and clauses, including FAR 52.212-1, FAR 52.212-2, FAR 52.212-4, and applicable FAR/HHSAR requirements, are incorporated by reference or provided in the solicitation and attachments. Prospective Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation, PWS, price schedule, and all attachments prior to submission. Proposals are due November 6, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. CT.

title: Intent to Sole Source: AFIT - High Finesse WS8-2 Wavemeter
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The United States Air Force, AFLCMC/PZIBA, Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio 45433-5344 publishes this notice of intent to award a sole source contract for informational purposes only. This proposed action is for the acquisition of a wavemeter for the Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT) located at Wright Patterson AFB, Ohio 45433. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO 6.103-1(b), �One responsible source. Agencies may contract without providing for full and open competition when the supplies or services required by the agency are available from only one responsible source and no other type of supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements,� resulting in a firm fixed price contract. The reason for lack of competition is as follows: The proposed vendor, Toptica Photonics Inc., is the only known source able to satisfy the Government's requirements. No other vendor has developed a wavemeter to the precision of Toptica's WS8-2. The primary factor in choosing this wavemeter is its capability to reliably measure a wavelength to <2 MHz. Other companies produce wavemeters that can be as low as 20 MHz in precision, but only Toptica guarantees accuracy down to 2 MHz. For this reason Toptica is the only company that meets all of the requirements. Both AFIT and contracting personnel utilized subject matter experts with experience for this requirement and vendor outreach but were unable to find other resources that were able to meet this requirement. The Contracting Officer has determined that only one source is reasonably available: Toptica Photonics Inc. title: Tybee Island Shoreline Protection Project
description: This presolicitation is for the Tybee Island Shoreline Protection Project. This acquisition is being offered as an unrestricted full and open competitive solicitation and will result in a single Firm Fixed- Price Contract Award. The construction magnitude for this project is between $10,000,000.00 and $25,000,000.00. Description of Work: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District, intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) to award a single firm fixed-price contract. Project work consists of placing dredged material along the Front Beach at Tybee Island, Georgia. The Contract includes a Base Bid item and Optional Bid items. The Base Bid item consists of placing berm fill material along approximately 7,000 feet of the construction baseline. Optional Bid items include placing additional material along the Front Beach area. The berm width varies along the project length. The Base Bid quantity is approximately 820,000 cubic yards of material and the four Option Bid items consist of approximately 673,000 cubic yards of material to be dredged for this renourishment. The material for the project will be sourced from an approved offshore borrow area that is approximately 5,000 feet away from the south end of the project and 11,000 feet from the center of the project. Work also includes environmental restrictions and beach tilling. The total construction duration for this project is 90 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). Evaluation Criteria: The contract will be solicited and procured using FAR Part 14 Sealed Bidding Procedures. Note: The Government anticipates issuing the invitation for bids on or after 06 November 2026. This date is estimated and subject to change. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be made available through the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/. Interested parties are encouraged to register as an interested vendor on SAM.gov to receive notifications of solicitation amendments. The Government is not responsible for notifying interested parties who have not registered or otherwise monitored SAM.gov for updates. Prospective bidders must be registered in SAM.gov at the time of bid submission and maintain an active registration through contract award, in accordance with FAR 52.204-7. The only authorized transmission method for a bid in response to this solicitation is electronically via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. NO OTHER TRANSMISSION METHODS (EMAIL, FACSIMILE, REGULAR MAIL, HAND CARRIED, ETC.) WILL BE ACCEPTED. The bids must be received by the Government by the date/time specified in the solicitation. Bidders shall submit their bid via the PIEE website Solicitation Module using the following link: https://piee.eb.mil/. Instructions on how to submit a bid can be found using the following link https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/sol/Posting_Offer.pdf. Contractual Questions should be forwarded to Contract Specialist, MSG Jeffrey Francisco at jeffrey.o.francisco.@usace.army.mil or to the attention of the Contracting Officer, Mr. Preston Jones at preston.e.jones@usace.army.mil.

description: Description: Mortgage-Backed Securities Operations & Analytics (MBSOA) The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is issuing this Sources Sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for providing Mortgage-Backed Securities Operations & Analytics (MBSOA) in Support of the Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) Office of Securities Operations (OSO). The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and Product Service Code (PSC) assigned to this procurement are: 541512 � Computer System Design Services with a size standard of $34M; and DA01 - IT And Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Support Services (Labor) There is no solicitation at this time. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. This is not an evaluation of proposals but an assessment of vendors� capabilities. Therefore, a high-level assessment of the capability statements will be performed. Generic brochures are not being requested. Vendors should provide information to stress their competencies, differentiators, and past performance showing or demonstrating their ability to fulfill PWS requirements. This requirement is set-aside for the General Services Administration (GSA) Aliant 3 Government-wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) holders. Each capability response must address the questions below. Responses that do not address the questions may not be evaluated or considered in the Government�s market research. Generic corporate brochures, marketing materials, or general descriptions of services that do not directly address the questions are insufficient. 1. Does your organization have experience working with government agencies such as Ginnie Mae, the Federal Housing Administration (FHA), Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) or the Office of Public and Indian Housing (PIH) providing services similar in scope, size and complexity as the Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements? 2. Does your organization possess the following special qualifications: an active Software Engineering Institute (SEI) CMMI Level III Certificate for Development, an active corporate ISO/IEC 20000 certification, an active corporate ISO 9001 (Quality Management) certification. 3. Describe your experience and current capability to support the MBSOA PWS services: 1) MBS Data Collection & Reporting services, 2) Information Technology services and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) services including Security and Enhancement activities, and 3) specialized MBS Risk and Information Analytic services. Include any related Ginnie Mae experience. Please indicate if your firm served as the prime contractor or subcontractor. 4. Provide examples of your company's experience supporting, managing, and modernizing a multi-platform, multi-provider environment that includes integrated legacy applications hosted in the cloud, while ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. 5. Provide an example where your firm improved operational efficiency, risk management, and information analytics capabilities, as well as investor reporting capabilities and accuracy for a client with similar requirements as this PWS within the secondary mortgage market or government-backed residential lending market. Include quantifiable results. 6. What are the three to five greatest risks associated with separating IT O&M from MBS business operations during contract period of performance, and what contractual, governance, technical, or operation controls would your company recommend to mitigate those risks? 7. Describe your company�s approach and protocol for maintaining 24/7/365 application and system availability, particularly during high-traffic events. Detail how your team identifies and mitigates technical challenges. 8. Based on your review of the PWS, are there any recommended changes, additions, or clarifications? Please identify the page number and paragraph. 9. Is your company able and willing to commit to providing services for a 10-year contract term? If not, please explain any limitations or concerns. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) organization name, address, email address, website address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) tailored capability statements addressing the questions and/or requested information listed above, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of personnel and risk mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. Based on the responses to this Sources Sought Notice/Market Research, this requirement may be further set aside for any of the socio-economic programs, set-aside for small business competition, procured through full and open competition, procured through GSA, etc. Interested potential offerors must clearly specify the following: their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), business size applicable to NAICS, socioeconomic business categories, GSA GWAC contract number, and any other applicable GWAC numbers. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION ATLANTIC INTRACOASTAL WATERWAY DISPOSAL AREA 60, ONSLOW COUNTY, NORTH CAROLINA This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information only. This is NOT a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. This request does not obligate the Government in any contract award. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Wilmington District, is conducting research to determine the market capabilities of potential contractors to perform a subsurface investigation for the purpose of collecting soil and strength parameters for the existing dike and foundation soils to complete slope stability analysis for the existing dike foundation soils. Disposal Area (DA) 60 is approximately 20 acres in size and located one and a quarter mile southeast of the NCWRC Cedar Point Boat Ramp, located in Cedar Point, North Carolina. Description of Services. The Contractor shall mobilize all necessary personnel, equipment, and materials to DA 60, to conduct a comprehensive geotechnical investigation. Methods of investigation should accurately locate changes in the soil strata. Equipment shall be able to traverse the site in wet, soft, or dry conditions. The following subsurface exploration and laboratory testing services will be required. Cone Penetration Test Sounding A total of eleven (11) CPT soundings shall be completed to a depth of 50 feet or refusal that occurs greater that 20 feet in depth, both within the crest of the existing dike structure, the interior of the existing dike structure, and waterside toe of the DA to assess soil stratigraphy and engineering properties. All work shall be completed in accordance with applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements, and coordinated with USACE representatives throughout the duration of the investigation. The Contractor shall be fully responsible for the transportation of all personnel, equipment, and materials to and from DA 60 for the duration of the geotechnical investigation. DA 60 is only accessible by water vessel; therefore, the Contractor must make all necessary arrangements for marine transportation to support field operations. No land access is available. 2. Site Information. Site maps, navigation charts and bathymetric maps may be acquired from the Wilmington District, Navigation Section. Historical tide data can be acquired from the NOAA Tides and Currents website; https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepredictions.html?id=8665728. Borehole coordinates will be provided by the Wilmington District for navigational purposes. 3. Water Vessel Requirements. All waterborne vessels shall be compliant with established US Coast Guard guidelines and regulations. 4. Field Work. As previously stated, this contract requires eleven (11) CPT soundings be conducted. All interested firms with 541360 as an approved NAICs code have until 6 November 2026 at 1500 ET to submit the following information: - Name & Address of your Firm - Point of Contact (Name/Phone/E-mail) - Current SAM - Business Size, to include designation as HUBZone, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Woman-Owned Business, and Large Business. Any supporting documentation that confirms your socio-economic status should be provided, i.e., letter of certification from VA confirming SDVOSB status. The Government must be able to verify SBA certification of HubZone and 8(a) via SAM. - Evidence of capabilities to perform comparable subsurface investigation work. The contractor must provide evidence of comparable work on two (2) recent projects (not more than seven (7) years old.) Include the project name and description of the key/salient features of the project (completion date, total contract value, and your company's level of involvement in the project, i.e., subcontractor (type), prime, GC, etc. and your specific role. Additionally, if you were teaming with another firm, clearly identify your role on the project(s) submitted. Please provide at least one point of contact (with e-mail address and phone number) for project validation. The Government will not give credit to projects if the lack of information hinders the ability to determine relevancy and/or level or experience. - Documentation of a drill rig that can perform CPT soundings as specified. The CPT equipment shall be pushed into the ground at a rate of 0.8 in/s. The CPT shall consist of a conical tip at the base of the rod for measuring the cone resistance and friction resistance every 0.8-inch interval. The cone shall have a base area of 1.6 in2, with a diameter of 1.4 in., and a height of 1.2 in., corresponding to a 60? apex angle. The cone is attached to a friction sleeve having a diameter of approximately 1.4 in. The tip of the cone is typically instrumented to measure the tip resistance using strain gauges, while the sleeve above the cone is instrumented to measure the sleeve friction. These parameters shall be used to obtain a profile of the variation of soil strength and soil type with depth. Additional instrumentation shall be attached to the cone to obtain additional data for correlation with other parameters such as porewater pressure. - Firm's capability to perform, to include geographic span and project size. - Information on Teaming Arrangement (if applicable). Although we are not looking for formal signed agreements at this time, if you intend to "team" with another firm, formally or informally, you must submit information, not more, than one (1) page, about your team's involvement. Any supporting documentation that confirms your socio-economic status as a team should be provided. The Government may not give credit to your socio-economic class if there is not sufficient documentation to support it or if the Government cannot verify through other means that your business is as such. description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE: OVERHAUL OF CATERPILLAR MARINE DIESEL ENGINE ONBOARD USCG CUTTERS. This SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE is for market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal/Quotation; and, it is not considered to be a commitment by the Government to award a contract nor will the Government pay for any information provided; no basis for claim against the Government shall arise as a result from a response to this Sources Sought Notice or Government use of any information provided. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: (1) Determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exists. (2) Determine if commercial items suitable to meet the agency's needs are available or could be modified to meet the agency's requirements. (3) Determine the commercial practices of company's engaged in providing the needed service or supply. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. REQUIREMENT: This notice is issued by the U.S. Coast Guard, CG-DCS-SEA-C, Base Alameda, CA to identify sources capable of providing the following: This acquisition is to provide Caterpillar (CAT) full service authorized/certified technical services to repair, perform maintenance on and or overhaul CAT ship�s service and main propulsion diesel engines onboard Coast Guard cutters based upon recommended original equipment manufacturer periodicity. The contractor must provide technical representative and engineering services, lube oil flushes, generator overhauls, and remanufactured main propulsion diesel engines for the Seagoing and Coastal Buoy Tenders (WLB & WLM), Inland and River Tenders (WLI, WLIC, &WLR), Tugs (WTGB & WYTL), 418-foot National Security Cutter (WSML), 360-foot Icebreaker (WAGB), 240-foot Icebreaker (WLBB), 282-foot (WMEC), 270-foot (WMEC), and 210-foot (WMEC) class vessels in accordance with OEM standards. The remanufactured Caterpillar Models are D348, D353, D379, D398, D3304, D3306, D3406, D3408, D3412, D3508, D3512, D3516, D3608, D3612, C18, C32, and C280-12. The remanufactured Caterpillar (CAT) Engines will include Computer Aided Marine Performance Analysis Report (CAMPAR) testing, engine timing synchronization, engine valve rotators, and vibration analysis. The government estimates 36-40 diesel engines will be serviced annually. USCG intends to award at least ten (10) Firm Fixed Price, Indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) Multi-Award-Task-Order Contracts (MATOC) on a brand name basis to the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Caterpillar Incorporated authorized dealers for remanufactured diesel engines. The intent of ten awards is to allow for coverage of USCG vessels dispersed throughout the United States, US territories, and outlying areas This acquisition shall be an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contracts for One Base year and Four Option Years, if exercised. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. title: DA01--RFI Action Only Healthcare Data Auditing Billing and Coding Optimization Software
description: Request for Information (RFI) Healthcare Data Auditing Billing and Coding Optimization Software - This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. Do not submit a quote. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), is conducting market research to inform a planned future acquisition. The intent is to gather information from qualified solution providers offering solutions to meet this critical business need. The Government seeks industry input on a modern, modular, cloud-based system capable of supporting the coding staff to collect health care data and accurately applying the codes to determine level of care provided to the patient population and ensure timely coding and revenue cycle activities on behalf of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). This notice is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. It shall not be construed as an Invitation for Bid, Request for Quotation, or Request for Proposal. This RFI does not commit the Government to any acquisition or contract award. Respondents will not be compensated for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information. No funds have been authorized or obligated for this requirement. All submissions become Government property. Respondents are responsible for marking proprietary information. VA does not want this market research to assume that today's current solution should simply be carried forward. VA is specifically seeking industry's perspective on how modern technology can meet the ability to provide this auditing, billing and coding capability across VHA. VA seeks industry feedback to inform future acquisition strategies for an enterprise-wide Healthcare Data Auditing Billing and Coding Optimization Software that enhances decision making, efficiency, supports VA coding professionals the ability to accurately and consistently code health care encounters and inpatient stays. Responses may support potential socioeconomic set-aside determinations; therefore, submissions should be complete, detailed, and accurate. Desired Outcomes Improve the accuracy, timeliness, consistency, and traceability of coding and billing activities. Provide configurable workflows for coding, clinical documentation integrity, billing, utilization review, compliance, and supervisory functions. Enable secure, standards-based, near-real-time or real-time exchange with Government clinical, scheduling, billing, identity, analytics, and enterprise data services. Provide enterprise, regional, facility, workgroup, and user-level reporting with auditable metrics. Reduce avoidable manual work, duplicate data entry, proprietary dependencies, and lifecycle cost. Maintain continuity of operations, cybersecurity, privacy, accessibility, and records-management compliance. Capability Requirements Enterprise Platform and User Experience An enterprise-capable solution or interoperable suite available to authorized users across geographically distributed facilities. Role-based access, configurable menus, work queues, dashboards, alerts, and administrative controls. A coherent user experience across coding, documentation integrity, billing, compliance, workflow, and reporting functions, while allowing modular components when beneficial. Support for large user populations and workload growth without per-user barriers that discourage adoption. Accessibility consists of applicable Federal information and communication technology requirements and compatibility with common assistive technologies. Coding and Encounter Management Support identification, assignment, review, coding, recoding, completion, and tracking of inpatient, outpatient, surgical, emergency, behavioral health, long-term care, and other encounters. Support current diagnosis, inpatient procedure, professional procedure, supply, dental, and other applicable code sets, including effective-date validation and version management. Validate code relationships, age, clinical attributes, modifiers, provider data, coverage, medical necessity, payer rules, and Government-configurable edits. Support code lookup and integration with one or more coding reference or encoder products through documented interfaces. Maintain status, assignment, reassignment, comments, communications, original values, changed values, user identity, reason, and date-time audit history. Clinical Documentation Integrity Provide independent, role-appropriate work queues for concurrent and retrospective review. Identify potential documentation improvement opportunities using configurable criteria and transparent logic. Create, route, communicate, and track documentation clarification requests and responses. Capture documentation-review codes, grouping results, severity, risk, expected length of stay, quality indicators, and comparison with final coded outcomes where applicable. Provide workload, response, impact, quality, and productivity reporting for documentation integrity programs. Billing, Claim Editing, and Compliance Provide institutional and professional claim review before and, where needed, after submission. Apply national, local, payer, technical, coding, medical necessity, provider identifier, present-on-admission, grouping, sequencing, and Government-defined edits. Support individual and batch claim review, transparent edit explanations, configurable messages, and authorized maintenance of custom rules. Identify incomplete, duplicate, non-billable, held, cancelled, retrospective-insurance, and same-day related encounters and preserve supporting rationale. Provide random and targeted sampling, compliance monitoring, complete audit trails, and exportable review results. Workflow and Auditability Provide configurable work assignment, prioritization, routing, escalation, suspense, alerts, and closure across organizational levels. Enable secure communication among coding, documentation integrity, billing, clinical, utilization review, compliance, supervisory, and technical personnel. Maintain tamper-evident or otherwise trustworthy audit history for user, system, rule, integration, and administrative actions. Permit authorized users to configure workflows and rules without vendor software development when feasible. Expose workflow data through documented interfaces and export mechanisms. Integration and Data Exchange Support bidirectional integration with the VistA electronic health record, legacy clinical, scheduling, admissions/discharge/transfer, surgery, clinical documentation, imaging report, laboratory, radiology, procedure, provider, identity, billing, and enterprise data services. Use documented, standards-based interfaces where practicable, including modern application programming interfaces and recognized health data exchange standards. Describe support for synchronous, asynchronous, event-driven, batch, and secure file exchange patterns, including reconciliation and error handling. Provide interface monitoring, message traceability, retry, alerting, testing, version control, and non-production environments. Allow the Government or a designated third party to integrate, automate, and extract data through appropriately secured interfaces without unnecessary contractual restrictions. Reporting, Analytics, and Data Portability Provide configurable dashboards, recurring reports, ad hoc analysis, data mining, filtering, sorting, alerts, and exports. Support enterprise, regional, facility, service, team, role, and user-level reporting for workload, timeliness, productivity, accuracy, quality, compliance, workflow, and revenue status. Integrate with Government analytics and enterprise data platforms, including common business intelligence tools. Provide complete, documented data dictionaries, lineage, metadata, refresh frequency, retention controls, and historical access. Enable Government-controlled export of transactional, audit, configuration, rule, reference, workflow, and reporting data in open, usable formats without additional extraction fees. Cyber

title: Department of War Office of the Assistant Secretary of War OASW(EI&E) Resilient Infrastructure and Layered Passive Survivability
description: Description. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI or reimburse any costs associated with the preparation of responses to this RFI. It will also not consider any solutions that are proprietary unless clearly marked. Overview. The Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Energy, Installations, and Environment (OASW(EI&E)) is soliciting concepts, capabilities, and technical insights from the military construction (MILCON), materials science, and defense-industrial sectors. The focus areas can be found in the attachment below. The Department of War (DoW) is transitioning its installation framework to support active operational posture. Under Title 10 of the U.S. Code and the strategic directives of the annual National Defense Authorization Act, military installations are recognized as primary power projection platforms. The survivability of these installations under kinetic and multi-domain threats is directly related to the readiness and capabilities of the U.S. Armed Forces. To support the development of the �Base of the Future,� the DoW seeks novel, non-prescriptive solutions in passive force protection to protect physical structures, personnel, and critical utility infrastructures. The Department intends to move past traditional �pour-concrete-and-hope� hardening and pivot the paradigm to focus on minimizing target signature, absorbing kinetic energy dynamically, and maintaining mission-essential functions even during active degradation. The DoW intends to use these insights to actively shape near-term procurement and long-term modernization strategies. Specifically, mature, ready-to-deploy technologies will be evaluated for immediate integration and inclusion in upcoming military construction standards. Promising, early-stage concepts will be used to guide and prioritize future research, development, and science and technology funding pipelines. Background. To identify potential technological advancements, the DoW seeks information categorized into four functional, capability-based domains. Respondents are encouraged to look beyond legacy building codes and focus on facility survivability in contested environments. Disclaimer: This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and strategic planning. This does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it obligate the Office of the Secretary of War or OASW(EI&E) to fund or contract for any submitted concepts.

title: JBMHH Gate Heaters & Fans Supply Rental
description: The Government intends to acquire a contract to provide eight (8) outdoor heaters and eight (8) misting fans, to be exchanged seasonally, for use at the access control points identified in the Specific Tasks section. All units will be operated outdoors and must be suitable for exposure to environmental elements. The Contractor shall provide, emplace, maintain, and recover all equipment. JBMHH will furnish fuel, water, and electricity necessary for operation. The Contractor shall inspect all equipment provided, including ensuring that all electrical cords are adequate and compatible with the required electrical supply. The contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, materials, and technical expertise required to perform diagnostics, repairs, replacements, and stabilization actions. Routine maintenance shall be conducted during standard business hours; however, the contractor must maintain continuous on-call support to respond to critical failures such as electrical hazards, complete equipment shutdown, or conditions that render the gate unsafe or inoperable. All work shall comply with applicable Army, DoD, and installation safety standards, ensuring uninterrupted support to access control operations.

When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. title: France – Sports goods and equipment – Fourniture et pose d'équipements sportifs dans les salles de gymnastique et de boxe dans le nouveau complexe sportif de Joinville-le-Pont
description: Le présent marché a pour objet l'achat et la pose d'équipements sportifs dans les salles de gymnastique et de boxe du nouveau complexe sportif de Joinville-le-Pont (94). Le marché est composé de deux lots : Lot 1 : Equipements sportifs de la salle de gymnastique - Lot 2 : Equipements sportifs de la salle de boxe. La liste des équipements attendus figure dans le CCTP de chaque lot. Le titulaire de chaque lot devra notamment assurer : - La fourniture des équipements sportifs neufs ; - La livraison à l'endroit indiqué par la commune dans le nouveau complexe sportif ; - La pose des équipements dans les conditions précisées dans les CCTP ; - La mise en service de ses équipements, les réglages et les essais ; - La réception des équipements. Le marché prend effet à compter de sa notification. Les différentes phases du marché seront exécutées dans le respect du planning prévisionnel figurant dans le dossier de consultation.

title: Vehicle Collision Repair, 2019 Ford F-150
description: The 144 FW ANG is issuing this pre-solicitation notice to identify qualified contractors for a service to repair vehicle body damage to a 2019 Ford F-150. This project requires automotive collision repair, associated substrate repair or replacement, and appropriate automotive paint. An RFQ is being considered as a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract and is anticipated under NAICS code 811121, Automotive Body, Paint, and Interior Repair and Maintenance. A specific socioeconomic category will be considered after marketplace review. If issued, award would be provided to the lowest responsive quoter. Interested quoters should provide the following: Business name, email, and phone contact. Cage Code or SAM UEI. Business SBA certified socioeconomic status(es). Website or capabilities statement. Address of automotive repair facility. Reference the pre-solicitation tile and number in the email subject header. Send information to jarrod.sanchez@us.af.mil

title: Multispectral Camouflage Overgarment
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & REQUIREMENT OVERVIEW: The Department of the Navy, United States Marine Corps, Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC), intends to compete a requirement for the manufacture, testing, and delivery of Multi-Spectral Camouflage Overgarment. This acquisition is set aside 100% for Small Business concerns under NAICS code 313310 and PSC Code 8415. The procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15 negotiated procedures for non-commercial supplies. 2. CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION (CUI) & CYBERSECURITY MANDATES: The technical specifications, Statement of Work (SOW), and Purchase Description (PD) associated with this requirement contain Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), specifically categorized as Controlled Technical Information (CTI). The resulting solicitation and contract will include strict information safeguarding requirements. To be eligible for award, offerors must comply with the following DFARS provisions and clauses, which will be incorporated into the solicitation: DFARS 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting DFARS 252.204-7019, Notice of NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements DFARS 252.204-7020, NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements Section III: SOW & Purchase Description (PD) Access Protocol The SOW and Purchase Description will not be publicly posted to SAM.gov. To obtain access to these restricted CUI/CTI documents, prospective offerors must complete the vetting process detailed in the table below: 1. Access Request: Submit an email request to the Contract Specialist with the subject line: "CUI Technical Package Request � M67854-27-R-5400 � [Company Name]". Must include Company Name, CAGE Code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and Point of Contact. 2. Cybersecurity & JCP Verification: Provide proof of an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) certification number (DD Form 2345) and verify that a NIST SP 800-171 self-assessment has been uploaded to the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). The Contracting Officer will independently verify SPRS scores and JCP status. Requests lacking active credentials will be rejected. 3. Execution of NDA: Sign and return the Government-furnished Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) governing the handling of CUI/CTI. Must be executed by an authorized corporate officer with binding authority. 4. Secure Distribution: Upon verification, the Government will transmit the SOW and Purchase Description. Direct email is prohibited. Delivery will occur exclusively via DoD SAFE (Secure Access File Exchange) using encrypted, password-protected links. Section IV: Submission of Questions & Inquiries Prospective offerors are authorized to submit questions regarding this pre-solicitation notice and the restricted technical package under the following strict conditions: Submission Deadline: Questions must be submitted in writing via email to the primary points of contact no later than (NLT) 1600 hours (4PM Eastern) on 06 November 2026. Format: Questions must be submitted using the Government-provided Q&A spreadsheet template (to be provided with the SOW/PD package) and must not contain proprietary or classified information. Disposition of Questions: Individual responses will not be distributed during the pre-solicitation phase. All questions resulting from this pre-solicitation notice will be consolidated, de-conflicted, and formally answered as an attachment to the final Request for Proposal (RFP) when issued.

title: Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. Failure Escalation & Root Cause Analysis: Describe your engineering experience and/or procedures for performing root cause failure investigations and delivering Failed Item Analysis Reports (FIARs) and
