title: AMS Designated Laboratory Meat Testing Services (ADL)
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is issuing Solicitation 12?1NTS?26?R?0002 to obtain proposals from responsible, accredited analytical laboratories to perform microbiological and fat testing in support of AMS meat, poultry, egg, and aquatic product procurement programs. This requirement establishes AMS Designated Laboratories (ADLs) responsible for conducting all required microbiological and chemical analyses on samples submitted by AMS vendors, ensuring compliance with Federal Purchase Program Specifications (FPPS) and supporting food safety and quality verification efforts. AMS intends to award an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) firm?fixed?price contract, consisting of a Base Period and up to four option periods, covering performance from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2032. Offerors must be fully capable of meeting all technical, accreditation, reporting, and quality assurance requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW) and must maintain ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for all applicable microbiological and chemical test methods throughout the contract term. Offerors are required to submit a complete proposal package in accordance with Section E of the solicitation, including all technical, management, past performance, and pricing components, as well as a properly completed and signed SF?1449. Offerors must ensure all requirements, instructions, and submission details�such as WBSCM electronic submission processes�are fully reviewed and followed. Incomplete proposals may not be considered for award. Key expectations under this solicitation include: � Performance of all required microbiological and fat analyses using approved methods (FSIS MLG, AOAC, AOCS, or AMS?approved alternatives). � Comprehensive sample preparation, receipt, testing, reporting, and data management in accordance with AMS SOW requirements. � Timely reporting of results, including notification of presumptive or confirmed pathogen positives to AMS, FSIS, and vendors. � Secure handling and management of proprietary AMS data. � Full compliance with FAR, AGAR, and USDA?specific contract clauses incorporated into the solicitation. Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged to read the entire solicitation package, including the SOW, exhibits, and all referenced clauses, to ensure a complete and conforming submission.

title: Water Resources Analytical and Professional Support Services - Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC)
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) intends to solicit for and negotiate several Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ)s styled as a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) using full and open competition under RFO (FAR) Part 15 procedures. The MATOC is anticipated to contain a period of performance consisting of one base year plus four one-year option periods and may include an option to extend the MATOCs for up to six-months to extend the contract in accordance with RFO 52.217-8. The anticipated maximum shared capacity of the MATOC is $49,500,000.00. A partial small-business set-aside is anticipated which will be determined by tasks in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The tasks to be set-aside are to be determined. Background: The USACE Institute for Water Resources (IWR) is a Field Operating Activity (FOA) under the Commanding General, USACE, and the staff supervision of the USACE Headquarters (HQUSACE) Directorate of Civil Works under the direction of the Deputy Commanding General for Civil and Emergency Operations (DCG-CEO) and the Director of Civil Works (DCW). IWR was established in 1969 to provide the USACE Civil Works (CW) Program with the capability to analyze and anticipate emerging water resources trends and issues facing our nation. From its beginning IWR has responded to the continuing changes in water resources development policies. IWR occupies a unique position within the USACE CW program and remains integral for insights into a host of complex and rapidly changing water resources issues. IWR operations are performed through these operating units: USACE Mission Support Battalion (UMSB) in Alexandria, VA; Hydrologic Engineering Center (HEC) in Davis, CA; Navigation and Civil Works Decision Support Center (NDC) co-located at the Humphreys Engineer Center (Alexandria, VA) and the USACE New Orleans District office in New Orleans, LA; Waterborne Commerce Statistics Center (WCSC) also located at the USACE New Orleans District office in New Orleans, LA Risk Management Center (RMC) co-located in Denver, CO and Pittsburgh, PA. IWR is the USACE center of expertise for integrated water resources management, focusing on planning analysis, hydraulic and hydrologic engineering, and on the collection, management and dissemination of Civil Works and navigation information, including the nation�s waterborne commerce data. IWR serves as the USACE center of expertise for dam and levee safety, analysis and adaptive management of water resources and infrastructure based on severe weather event data, planning, and environmental conflict resolution. IWR also operates the International Center for Integrated Water Resources Management (ICIWaRM), under the auspices of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). IWR fulfills its mission by providing: (a) analysis of emerging and long-term water resources and waterborne transportation trends, needs and issues, (b) state-of-the-art planning and hydrologic engineering methods, models and training, (c) policy and program analyses and strategic planning to support and improve the effectiveness and efficiency of CW program. Among the specific purposes stated, delivered services will require consideration of data and analytical requirements of the USACE�s CW water resources missions to include the areas of study and expertise that IWR provides to its customers through its research, analysis, technical assistance and training activities to include but not limited to Navigation, Flood and Storm Damage Reduction, Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration, Emergency Management, Water Supply, Hydropower and Recreation. IWR routinely provides technical assistance on a broad range of topic areas to USACE Headquarters and the Major Subordinate Commands (divisions, districts, and laboratories), other US Army Commands, federal and state agencies, foreign nations, and international organizations. Description of the Requirement: This MATOC will obtain products and professional services through technical research and analytical support, data management, facilitation, and training for IWR that is generally not readily available within the USACE. These services will be used by IWR to accomplish missions including but not limited to: Support, operation, maintenance, upkeep, enhancement, and development of Automated Information Systems (AIS) and applications operated and/or otherwise managed by IWR and its various centers. These services will require consideration of data and analytical requirements of the USACE�s CW water resources missions to include the areas of study and expertise that IWR provides to its customers. These systems include: a. Analysis of emerging trends and issues in anticipation of changing water resources management conditions and the corporate development of policies, programs b. Systems-based planning methodologies, tools and training across the CW portfolio for analysis, economic and socio-economic assessments. c. Project-, regional- and national-level economic analysis, multi-criteria and risk-informed analysis, economic and socio-economic assessments: d. State of the art hydrologic and hydraulic engineering tools, methodologies, models and management systems and associated planning and environmental methods, models and training. e. Advanced engineering risk management expertise for dam, levee and infrastructure safety, and the development, application and stewardship of the engineering practice involving contemporary risk-related methods, models and training. f. Support for USACE to anticipate, prevent or minimize water conflicts and coastal flood risk g. Support for the USACE Community of Practice for Conflict Resolution and Public Participation to lead facilitation for stakeholder support. h. Expertise on water security and Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) applied by the U.S. State Department, United Nations, other U.S. and international institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), to address water and natural resources planning, water policy and governance, water management, trans-boundary water conflict mitigation, and other water-related challenges within the U.S. and around the world. i. Assistance to HQUSACE, Army, and DoW, working in partnership with USACE MSCs and DoW COCOMs, for strengthening theater security cooperation by facilitating civilian and military collaborations, emphasizing multi-national force capacity development on the life-cycle planning of the humanitarian response and consequence management across all forms of extreme water events and other natural and technological disasters. j. A critical mass of knowledge on the engineering and scientific aspects of, extreme weather events, and other risk factors in collaboration with interagency partners and study development k. Enterprise-level financial analysis expertise in support of the CW mission and USACE intergovernmental collaboration on public works infrastructure investment decisions. Development and sustainment of USACE financial programs such as CWIPF This support will include assistance and guidance related to the outreach, accounting, project and borrower eligibility screening, FCRA compliance, and related efforts necessary for successful implementation of the federal credit program (including through its existing partnership with EPA to help develop and implement CWIFP) . l. Technical support to USACE on a wide range of water resources, marine transportation, flood/coastal storm risk reduction, conflict resolution, international water and natural resources stewardship and ecosystem management issues. Scope: The scope of this contract includes all of the Civil Works mission areas (i.e. Navigation, Flood Risk Management, Aquatic Ecosystem Restoration, Hydropower, Regulatory, Recreation, and Water Supply) providing capability for technical research and analysis, data management, training and facilitation activities, among other tec

description: UPDATE - 10/07/2026 The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) John F. Kennedy Space Center is pleased to release the 2027 NASA Agency-wide Acquisition of Nitrogen and Oxygen (NANO) 4 opt-in opportunity as described in the original NANO 4 Request for Proposal (RFP), Sections 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 RFP was issued on March 4, 2024, and the original solicitation (as revised) remains open throughout the ordering period through the use of innovative provisions as prescribed in Section 2, Clause 2.9, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in, and Clause 2.9.2, IDIQ CLIN Pool Opt-in After Award. The NANO 4 contract�s ordering period remains valid through June 30, 2029. The RFP resulted in the award of six indefinite delivery (ID) fixed price with Economic Price Adjustment (FPEPA) requirements contracts with fixed price delivery orders for the supply of liquid nitrogen and liquid oxygen in support of operations at agency centers and facilities across the United States. NASA made award to the following companies: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc., Airgas USA LLC (Central), Airgas USA LLC (South), Linde, Inc., Nippon Sanso Matheson, Inc. (formerly Matheson Tri-gas, Inc.), and Messer LLC. Each year during the life of the solicitation and at the time established via synopsis, the Government will accept proposals from new entrants for each IDIQ subCLIN location and the Government will also accept proposals from existing NANO 4 contractors for each additional proposed IDIQ subCLIN location. A new entrant does not hold a current NASA liquid nitrogen or liquid oxygen contract. The Government will evaluate the proposals to determine technical acceptability for a specific NASA location. Upon the Government�s determination of technical acceptability, a contract (for new entrants) or contract modification (for existing NANO 4 Contractors) will be executed to add the Contractor to the IDIQ CLIN Pool for the specific NASA location. Thereafter, the Contractor will be eligible to participate in the IDIQ CLIN Pool process described in Section 2.8 for the NASA locations awarded to that Contractor. All eligible Contractors who are awarded an IDIQ subCLIN for a particular NASA location will have the option to compete for requirements within those IDIQ subCLINs which they are awarded. title: MQ-25 BOA Readiness and Sustainment Support
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Patuxent River, MD, intends to negotiate and award a Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) Task Order for interim readiness and sustaining, logistics, and engineering support for the MQ-25A productionized representative Engineering Demonstration Model (EDM), System Demonstration Test Article (SDTA), SDTA+, and Low- Rate Initial Production (LRIP) air vehicles under the MQ-25A Program. The proposed contract action(s) identified above are those for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(l) and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other type of supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Boeing is the sole designer, developer, and manufacturer of the MQ-25 Air System and therefore, Boeing is the only contractor that can successfully deliver the system without an unacceptable schedule delay in fulfilling the U.S. Navy's requirements. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. Interested parties, however, may identify their interest and capability by responding to the requirement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this synopsis. Information received will be considered solely for determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract actions based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses shall be made in writing by E-Mail to the Points of Contact identified in this notice. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities are encouraged to contact Boeing directly via Brad Westerfeld, at bradley.r.westerfeld@boeing.com.

title: 2027 US AND UK WEAPON CONTROL SYSTEM SPARES AND SPECIAL SUPPORT EQUIPMENT
description: The Strategic Systems Programs (SSP) intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) and negotiate an Order under existing BOA N0003025G1038, issued on a sole source basis to General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS), Pittsfield, MA. Work shall include procuring, inspecting and testing U.S. and UK Weapon Control System Spares and Special Support equipment spare parts listed as deliverables for the Fire Control System (FCS) Auxiliary System (AS) including the Strategic Weapons System Maintenance Information Network (SWSMIN), Electronic Work Log (EQL) and associated Fire Control Support Equipment. Weapon Control System Spares and Special Support Equipment spare parts shall be procured and delivered in accordance with the applicable Ordnance Directives (ODs), Technical Program Management processes, and Statement of Work (SOW). Award will be made using other than full and open competition to General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS), Pittsfield, Massachusetts, the only known source with the requisite design background, system knowledge and operational experience relative to the TRIDENT II Fire Control Subsystem capable of providing the required efforts within existing technical, cost and fleet schedule constraints. No Solicitation package is available. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. No email or phone inquiries will be entertained. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS), Pittsfield, MA, Small Business Liaison, Ms. Alexis Petro via email at alexis.petro@gd-ms.com.

title: AN/SPN-50(V) Engineering Development Model Contract
description: 1. INTRODUCTION THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible businesses capable of providing the supplies/services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a possible Request for Proposal. Interested parties will be required to respond separately to any solicitations posted as a result of this sources sought notice. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources because of this notice. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 BACKGROUND The Naval Air Command (NAVAIR) requires an upgrade the AN/SPN-50(V) Radars due to obsolescence issues. The procurement will be for one (1) Engineering Development Model (EMD) Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR) asset. The EDM system is essential for environmental and qualification testing. This procurement will ensure we meet the production and delivery schedule need. This effort will require contractor support for the testing and installation. 4.0 REQUIRED CAPABILITIES NAVAIR requires delivery of the EMD unit within 3 months to allow sufficient time to complete environmental and qualification testing within 36 months as well as Contractor support for testing and installation of the EMD. Specialized skills are required for the production effort to meet the stringent schedule to field future qualified Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR)s on Carrier, Heavier-than-air-aviation, Nuclear-Powered (CVN), Landing Helicopter Dock (LHD), and Landing Helicopter Assault (LHA) ships by FY30. This EMD unit shall leverage current AN/SPN-50(V) systems because of similarity within units and similar system structure, as well as consistent theory of operation developed by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). This EMD unit is required to fit within the same footprint as the current AN/SPN-50(V) system and be 100 percent compatible with current interfaces to external systems. The AN/SPN-50(V) includes integration of complex contractor developed software and hardware in conjunction with Government cooperation using organically developed algorithms for target processing. This system is specialized for operation with the AN/SYY-1 Display system, involving characterization of the system in their operational environment to ensure ship requirements are met. The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is the sole AN/SPN-50(V) designer, developer and manufacturer. The U.S. Navy did not procure the Technical Data Package (TDP) that would allow another source to produce the AN/SPN-50. Interested parties must include a detailed explanation of how they would complete the production requirements without a Government furnished TDP. Any responses must explain how they will meet delivery schedules. 5.0 INCUMBENT The OEM is Saab Defense and Security, USA, LLC 5717 Enterprise Parkway, East Syracuse, NY 13057-2963. 6.0 ELIGIBILITY All interested contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management government website at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of Government contracts. Only interested firms who possess the supplies and services provided in this notice and can meet these requirements are invited to respond. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this notice. 7.0 SUBMITTAL INFORMATION It is requested that interested vendors submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 10 - 8.5 x 11 pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum) demonstrating the capability to meet the requirements of this notice. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: A company profile to include Company name, business size under NAICS Code 334511, office location(s), Point of Contact name, phone number, email address, Commercial and Government Entity code, and Unique Entity ID. Include a brief description of any applicable contracts relating to the supplies and/or services described herein. Prior/current industry experience of similar size and scope as referenced in section 3.0 �Required Capabilities�. Address the proposed management approach to staffing the effort with qualified personnel. Include corporate management policies, quality certifications, and the experience level of currently employed personnel to be assigned tasks under this effort. Provide documentation of the company's ability to begin performance immediately upon contract award projected in Q1FY25, to include a detailed plan and estimated schedule(s) of performance. Include any deviation or impact, if applicable. Provide documentation to show the company's ability to meet the Required Capabilities and Eligibility of this notice. Media: One (1) electronic copy is required. Submissions should be in Adobe PDF. Note that large files (>5MB) may not be receivable due to the Navy Marine Corps Intranet security. Means of Delivery: Submissions must be received no later than the Response Date of this notice. The capability statement package and/or questions or comments regarding this notice may be sent by email to Denise Pearch at denise.a.pearch.civ@us.navy.mil.

Description The Government intends to issue a solicitation for construction services for the Hattiesburg Court Security Construction Project at the William M. Colmer Federal Building, located at 701 North Main Street in Hattiesburg, Mississippi. The project is anticipated to include construction, renovation, alteration, and security-related improvements to support court operations and building security requirements. title: Integrated GOTS/NDI Systems and COTS Modular Enablers & Building Blocks
description: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Tech Transition Office AFRL/RR, in coordination with the Information and Spectrum Warfare Directorate (AFRL/RI), is seeking information from industry to improve USAF understanding of domestic market capabilities and identify qualified vendors to collaborate with. Specifically, AFRL is investigating technologies small enough to be installed on Group 2-3 unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) across two core pathways: 1. Integrated GOTS/NDI Systems: Existing Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) or Non- Developmental Item (NDI) radar electronic attack (EA) systems that have been proven or demonstrated for military use. 2. COTS Modular Enablers & Building Blocks: Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) hardware, open software-defined architectures, and high-performance RF components. AFRL is highly interested in innovative commercial building blocks�including Radio Frequency System on Chip (RFSoC) technology, high-speed analog-to-digital converters, and edge compute chips�that can support receive, process, and transmit capabilities in a variety of active and passive military scenarios.

title: Massachusetts Army National Guard Tailoring & Alterations
description: The Massachusetts Army National Guard (MAARNG) requires tailoring and alterations of the Army Service Uniform (ASU) and Army Green Service Uniform (AGSU) for its Soldiers. Services must be performed in accordance with Army Regulation (AR) 670-1 and DA PAM 670-1. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) will establish a streamlined method for ordering these recurring services. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as Government Furnished, to perform Army Service Uniform (ASU) and Army Green Service Uniform (AGSU) Tailoring and Alteration Services, as defined in this PWS. IMPORTANT: All quoters must read and adhere to the detailed instructions provided in the "Addendum to 52.212-1 - Instructions to Offerors" contained within the solicitation package. This addendum provides specific requirements for quote preparation, content, and submission that are essential for a quote to be considered for award. Submission and Award Information Quote Submission: All quotes must be submitted via email to both Marc Kerrigan and Melissa Melcher at the email addresses listed. Quote Deadline: The closing date and time are specified in Block 8 of the attached SF 1449. Late submissions will not be evaluated. Question Deadline: All questions must be submitted via email to both contacts no later than five (5) business days prior to the closing date. Basis for Award The Government intends to award to multiple vendors via a Blanket Purchase Agreement. The award will be made to the responsible quoters submitting the lowest total price for all CLINs, whose quote conforms to all solicitation requirements. The Government will evaluate quotes by first ranking all quotes by price. It will then evaluate the lowest-priced quotes for technical acceptability. If the lowest-priced quotes are technically acceptable and submitted by a responsible quoter, an award will be made within the limits of the Blanket Purchase Agreement. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site for any amendments to the solicitation. All interested and responsible small businesses may submit a quote,which shall be considered by the agency. Please download the attached solicitation documents for full details and instructions.

title: Engineering Services for the B-52H Stratofortress
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL/QUOTE. This synopsis is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract nor does the Government intend to directly pay for any information or responses submitted as a result of this solicitation. This is a Sources Sought Synopsis; there is no solicitation available at this time. This Sources Sought Synopsis is published for market research purposes only. Companies may be contacted if further information is needed. This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Synopsis to seek a contractor for future work pertaining to the B-52H engineering services starting 01 January 2028. The Boeing B-52H Stratofortress is an American long-range subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber. The B-52 was designed and built by Boeing, which has continued to provide support and upgrades. It has been operated by the United States Air Force (USAF) since 1955 and was flown by NASA from 1959 to 2007. The bomber can carry up to 70,000 pounds (32,000 kg) of weapons and has a typical combat range of around 8,800 miles (14,200 km) without aerial refueling. The sustainment of the B-52H currently includes the delivery of engineering design, engineering support, and technical support services crucial for the ongoing maintenance and operational readiness of the B-52H aircraft, including its components and associated support and test equipment. The original estimated minimum/maximum amount for the B-52H sustainment contracts was $1.15B over ten (10) years (2019-2028) for engineering services Contract efforts are subject to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.232-18 availability of funds. The sustainment contracts currently contain multiple contract types at the contract line-item level (e.g. firm fixed price, cost plus incentive fee, cost plus fixed fee, etc.) This Sources Sought Synopsis only addresses the B-52H engineering services requirements starting 01 January 2029. The contractor will be required to provide engineering support services that provide technical information and logistics resources to enable maintenance and operational readiness of 76 B-52H aircraft. Engineering services will be required at the following USAF operational bases: Tinker AFB, Oklahoma; Edwards AFB, California; Minot AFB, North Dakota, and Barksdale AFB, Louisiana. Additionally, the contractor shall provide engineering support at the Boeing facility Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, to reflect field service representative (FSR) support. The contractor will be required to perform the following recurring engineering services: - Program Management and Integration - Principal Point of Contact - Platform Website - Meetings, briefings, conferences, reviews, and Technical Interchange Meeting (TIMs) - Structures Working Group - Government Property and Material Management - Unique Identifier (UID) Requirements - Configuration Management - Data management, automation and Contract data Requirements Delivery (CDRL) and CDRL Quality - Engineering Data/Documents Files - Quality Assurance Program - Engineering Support - Aircraft Structural Integrity Program (ASIP) - Specialized Engineering Support - System Integration Lab (SIL) - Ground and Flight Test Engineering Support - Drawing Cleanup and Procurement Ready Drawing - Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) Repair Development - Voluntary Protection Program - Field Services Representative (FSR) The contractor will be required to perform the following Non-recurring Engineering (NRE) services support: - Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Statement of Work (SOW) - Expedited Acquisitioin Process (EAP) and Engineering Projects (EP) - Interim Contractor Support (ICS) - Over & Above (O&A) - Travel - Material - Data Requirements - Meetings, briefings, conferences, reviews, and Technical Interchange Meeting (TIMs) - Associate Contractors and Proprietary Information Agreements (PIA) - Quality Assurance and Quality Management System - Safety - System Engineering - Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) - Earned Value management (EVM)s - Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) It is critical that respondents include the degree to which they will require access to B-52H rights and the degree to which they have or are able to obtain B-52H rights from Boeing. The capabilities package should be brief and concise yet clearly demonstrate an ability to meet the stated requirements. Recent, relevant experience should be provided for each area. If a company is capable of some, but not all of the consolidated requirements stated in this Sources Sought Synopsis, please provide a response that explains the requirements for which you are capable. Teaming and/or subcontracting arrangements should be clearly delineated and previous experience in teaming must be provided. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this action is 541330, size standard is $25.5 million. Firms responding to this announcement should indicate whether they are a large business, other than small business, small business, small disadvantaged business (SDB), woman-owned small business (WOSB), economically disadvantaged women-owned small business (EDWOSB), 8(a)-certified business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), or Historically Underutilized Business Zone small business (HUBZone). All prospective contractors shall be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database to be awarded a DoD contract. title: 380 kV, Bonaduz-Sils (GR), remplacement des pylônes avifaune
description:
Les travaux de génie civil comprennent la réalisation ou le renforcement des fondations pour huit emplacements de pylônes. Pour sept pylônes, les fondations existantes seront agrandies, assainies et renforcées au moyen de micropieux. En raison de sa proximité avec un cours d’eau de surface, le pylône 1261x005 sera déplacé d’environ 40 m en direction du pylône 1261x004 et sera doté, à son nouvel emplacement, d’une fondation entièrement nouvelle renforcée au moyen de micropieux. Le pylône 1261x005 sera en outre rehaussé de 4 m et le pylône 1261x019 de 9 m.

L’étendue des prestations comprend notamment les travaux de démolition et de sécurisation nécessaires, l’aménagement des accès au chantier et des voies d’accès temporaires, les travaux d’excavation et de stabilisation des talus, la réalisation de micropieux, les travaux de bétonnage et de fondation, les travaux de mise à la terre ainsi que la remise en état complète des surfaces utilisées. Les montants d’angle des nouveaux pylônes de la ligne seront scellés dans les fondations en béton.

Les travaux seront réalisés en partie dans des zones sensibles du point de vue paysager et écologique ainsi que sur des terrains difficiles d’accès et escarpés. Les prescriptions spécifiques à chaque site concernant la protection de la nature, du paysage, des eaux et des sols, ainsi que les surfaces autorisées pour les accès, les installations de chantier et les travaux, doivent impérativement être respectées lors de l’exécution.


Pour des raisons géographiques, l’appel d’offres relatif aux travaux de génie civil est subdivisé en deux lots, comprenant chacun quatre emplacements de pylônes.


L’étendue détaillée des prestations ainsi que les exigences et les quantités spécifiques au projet figurent dans les documents d’appel d’offres.

title: Planificateur général SIA 32-53 pour la sous-station de Regensdorf
description:
La sous-station de 220 kV de Regensdorf est située dans la commune de Regensdorf, dans le canton de Zurich.


L'installation de commutation de 220 kV à isolation gazeuse de la sous-station de Regensdorf a été mise en service en 2021. Malgré le jeune âge de l'installation à isolation gazeuse (5 ans), celle-ci ne peut pas, selon le fabricant, être étendue avec le même type d'installation. Une pièce d'adaptation fabriquée sur mesure est nécessaire pour pouvoir procéder à l'extension vers un type d'installation actuel. Cela s'accompagne d'un besoin d'espace plus important, raison pour laquelle Swissgrid a décidé d'agrandir directement l'installation de deux baies. À cette fin, l'installation GIS doit être agrandie de deux baies (baie de transformateur et baie de réserve), ainsi que des raccordements de câbles nécessaires.


Le présent appel d'offres vise à recruter le planificateur général pour les phases SIA 32 à 53 afin d'assurer la planification et la coordination de ce projet, les phases SIA 51 à 53 étant attribuées à titre optionnel. Outre l'étendue des prestations spécifiques à son domaine de compétence, le maître d'œuvre assume également la supervision et la coordination générales de tous les domaines spécialisés impliqués, y compris les interfaces associées, en tant que responsable général au sens de la norme SIA 103.


Les sous-projets suivants doivent être organisés par le planificateur général:


  • Direction et coordination de tous les domaines spécialisés impliqués, y compris les interfaces
  • Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet - Techniques des circuits primaires
  • Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet - Besoins propres
  • Ingénierie et planification dans le sous-projet - Bâtiment et génie civil
  • Direction des trauvaux (facultatif)


Les sous-projets suivants sont mis à la disposition du planificateur général:


  • Coordination générale des modèles BIM
  • Ingénierie et planifcation dans le sous-projet - Système d'automatisation des sous-stations (SAS)
  • Conception et planification dans le sous-projet - Environnement



Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter les documents C100 et C101 du dossier d'appel d'offres.

title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Stadt Cottbus - VHVmöTw 207-2026 Entwicklung Gesamtschulstandort Joliot-Curie-Straße/Gartenstraße in Cottbus - Planungsleistung Technische Ausrüstung (ELT)
description: Die gewählten städtischen Flächen zur Entwicklung eines Gesamtschulstandortes mit Gymnasialer Oberstufe bieten sich aufgrund der bereits vorhandenen Infrastruktur bestens an. Auf dem zur Verfügung stehenden Gelände befindet sich entlang der Joliot-Curie-Straße bereits ein Gebäuderiegel, der schon zu DDR- Zeiten eine Polytechnische Oberschule beherbergte und derzeit für die Schule des Zweiten Bildungsweges genutzt wird. Entlang der Gartenstraße rahmt ein weiteres Gebäude das ca. 19.000m2 große Areal, dass zur Planung des neuen Schulstandortes zur Verfügung steht. Einst als Datenverarbeitungszentrum später als Erweiterte Oberschule bzw. Gymnasium genutzt, ist das 1969 in Betrieb gegangene Gebäude strukturell für schulische Zwecke geplant und genutzt worden. Nach Jahren des Leerstandes befindet sich momentan ein Hort in der Immobile, der auf Teilflächen ein Betreuungsangebot für Kleinkinder anbietet. Komplettiert wird der vorhandene Gebäudekomplex von einer kleinen Sporthalle, deren Errichtungszeitraum, wie bei den Schulgebäuden, in die Zeit zum Ende der 1960er Jahre einzuordnen ist. Aktuell nutzen Vereine die räumlichen Kapazitäten für ihren Trainingsbetrieb. Die genauen Angaben entnehmen Sie bitte der Leistungsbeschreibung.

title: Germany – Security services – Empfangs- und Sicherheitsdienstleistungen
description: Das Deutsche Institut für Ernährungsforschung Potsdam-Rehbrücke (DIfE) erforscht den Einfluss der Ernährung auf die Gesundheit, mit dem Ziel, wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse für Prävention und Therapie ernährungsbedingter Erkrankungen nutzbar zu machen. Um neue Lösungsansätze aus dem Labor schnellstmöglich zum Menschen zu bringen, arbeiten die Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler in einer Kombination von experimenteller und angewandter Forschung: Von Zelle und Maus, über epidemiologische Beobachtungen, bis hin zu humanen Interventionen. Das DIfE beabsichtigt Empfangs- und Sicherungsdienstleistungen nach § 34a GewO und sicherungstechnische Überwachungsleistungen im Objektschutz gemäß nachfolgender Ausschreibung zum 21.02.2027 an einen externen Dienstleister zu vergeben. Die ordnungsgemäße Übernahme der Leistung vom bisherigen Dienstleister ist Bestandteil der Ausschreibung, eine entsprechende Übernahmephase ist mit auszuweisen. Die Leistungsdauer beträgt zwei Jahre mit der Option einer zweimaligen Verlängerung um jeweils 12 Monate. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind personelle Sicherungsdienstleistungen im Objektschutz in Form der betrieblichen Objektbewachung mit Tor- und Empfangsdienst sowie Streifen- und Interventionsdienst, der Bewachung und Überwachung von Forschungs-, Büroeinrichtungen und Lagern. Dazu zählt die Prävention gegen alle Formen potentieller Angriffe insbesondere auf die Objekte und ihren Inhalt, das Eigentum und Vermögen mit Intervention bei Alarmmeldungen sowie sonstigen Vorkommnissen. An die interne und externe Intervention werden besondere qualitative Ansprüche gestellt.
